html:
A bishop and writer from Roman North Africa whose books shaped Western Christian thought more than any others after the Bible. He was born at Thagaste, in what is now Algeria, to a Christian mother, Monica.

As a young teacher of rhetoric in Carthage, Rome and Milan he followed Manichaeism and then Neoplatonism. In Milan in 386 he turned to Christianity, and he was baptised the next year. From about 396 until his death he was bishop of Hippo, a port on the African coast of the Roman Empire.

His Confessions tells the story of his inner life and his conversion, one of the first great autobiographies. After the Visigoths' sack of Rome in 410, pagans blamed the Christian God, and he answered with The City of God, which sets God's eternal city against the passing cities of this world. Building on Paul, he taught that people are saved by God's grace, not their own effort, and he shaped ideas of original sin and just war.

He died in 430 as the Vandals, who had crossed into Africa, besieged Hippo. Both Catholics and the leaders of the Reformation claimed him.
sum: A bishop and writer from Roman North Africa whose books shaped Western Christian thought more than any others after the Bible. He was born at Thagaste, in what is now Algeria, to a Christian mother, Monica.
